{"name":"pr4d/hvar-advances","commit":{"sha":"56c39581392535e0c45055225889a9e4e889ee71","node_id":"C_kwDOAORW-9oAKDU2YzM5NTgxMzkyNTM1ZTBjNDUwNTUyMjU4ODlhOWU0ZTg4OWVlNzE","commit":{"author":{"name":"Benedikt Stebner","email":"Gillibald@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-09-07T07:48:02Z"},"committer":{"name":"Benedikt Stebner","email":"Gillibald@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-09-29T13:47:42Z"},"message":"Pre-compute HVAR region scalers per clone

An ItemVariationStore's regions are fixed for the font's lifetime, and a
varied clone's active coordinates are fixed for the clone's, so the
per-region scaler that the inner delta loop recomputes for every glyph is
the same value every call. Compute the vector once at clone construction
and the per-glyph HVAR lookup becomes an array index instead of a per-axis
F2DOT14 ramp.

Measured on a paragraph-size batch advance lookup (i7-12700K, .NET 10):
single glyph 52.0 ns -> 16.6 ns, batch 200 11.2 us -> 2.9 us, batch 2000
108.7 us -> 28.9 us. Per-glyph HVAR overhead drops from 55 ns to 14.6 ns,
which takes the gap to Skia's GetGlyphWidths from roughly 9x to 2.5x at
batch 200. Static and default-instance callers are unaffected: the gating
check reads _hvarRegionScalers instead of _activeCoords, and both are null
on that path.

ItemVariationStore gains ComputeRegionScalers and TryGetDeltaWithScalers;
the coordinate-based TryGetDelta stays for callers that have no
precomputed vector, such as MVAR's clone-time metric application, which
runs before the scalers exist.
